SAI will close and unsaved work will be lost. Open the SAI Pen screen?
Menu: tap with four fingers, or the back gesture. Keyboard: tap with three fingers.

These are the standard gestures; change them under Gestures on this screen, or hold four fingers still over SAI. Every gesture as it is set now: About SAI Pen at the bottom of this screen.

Pen: draws, with pressure. The pen's side button held while touching: right click.

One finger: puts the cursor under it; a short tap clicks.

Two fingers: move them to scroll the canvas, spread or pinch them to zoom, turn them to rotate the canvas. A short tap: right click.

Three fingers, a short tap: the keyboard, to type a file name. Held still for a moment: show or hide the on-screen keys.

Four fingers, a short tap, or the back gesture from the screen edge: the menu, with the keyboard, "SAI Pen: licence and settings" and Exit. Held still for a moment: the gesture settings, right over SAI.

Closing SAI with its cross brings you back to this screen.
SAI closed. Back to SAI Pen

Without a licence SAI works as a trial: it does not save or open files.\n\nSAI Pen can look for the licence file (named sai….slc) in Downloads and in SAI\'s folder. It reads only that file and copies it into SAI\'s own folder inside this app; nothing is sent anywhere. Or choose the file yourself.
No licence file (sai*.slc) in Downloads or SAI\'s folder. To get one: start SAI, menu Other, System ID, and download a certificate for that System ID on the SYSTEMAX site.
Found the SAI licence %1$s in %2$s, and using it
Start SAI right away when SAI Pen opens

SAI on this device has its own System ID, so a licence certificate made for another computer or device does not work here. You do not buy SAI again:

1. Start SAI and open Other, System ID.
2. On the SYSTEMAX site enter your licence number, password and that System ID, and download the certificate (sai….slc).
3. Leave it in Downloads: at the next start SAI Pen copies it into SAI by itself. It reads only that file; nothing is sent anywhere.

SAI Pen reinstalled on this same device? The System ID stays the same: choose your earlier certificate with Choose the file.
SAI\'s screen sharpness. Higher is sharper, but slower and with smaller buttons.
Tip: a short tap with three fingers opens the keyboard, and another one closes it.
Tip: hold three fingers still for a moment to show or hide the on-screen keys.
SAI is starting, %1$d s. The first start takes longer.
SAI is drawing its window, %1$d s
Make a timelapse video (%1$d frames, about %2$d s)
Delete the %1$d recorded frames without making a video? The next timelapse starts from scratch. This can\'t be undone.
The video did not work out: %1$s
Palm rejection: each check works on its own
Ignore touches Android marks as a palm
Ignore fingers while the pen is near, and 1.5 s after
Ignore large touches, like the side of a hand
This one can get in the way of two-finger gestures (zoom, move, rotate): while the pen is near, fingers are not noticed at all. Turn it on only if the other two did not help.
Keep speed logs, to compare the choices
With a front buffer, bits of the picture can stay on the screen (for example the brush circle while the pen hovers), more often on slower devices. If you see them, choose Standard.

The front buffer while the pen is near the screen or drawing, and Standard for menus, zooming and scrolling. Ink comes as soon as with the front buffer; everything else is as smooth as Standard. How the front buffer looks depends on the device: if bits of the brush circle stay on the screen while the pen hovers, choose Standard. Takes effect the next time SAI starts.

SAI\'s picture goes straight onto the screen, without waiting in Android\'s queue, so the ink comes sooner. How it looks depends on the device: if the picture flickers or tears, or bits of the brush circle stay on the screen while the pen hovers, choose Standard. Devices that can\'t do it use Standard by themselves. Takes effect the next time SAI starts.
Every picture waits in Android\'s queue before it is shown, as in other apps: a little more lag, but never a half-drawn picture. Takes effect the next time SAI starts.
The threads that draw get the fast cores. Menus and the rest of SAI stay as before.
All of SAI on the fast cores. Drawing is fastest, but menus may be slower.
SAI runs on every core, as Android decides.
Pen to screen in past sessions. Less is faster.
This device has no slow cores: nothing to choose.
All %1$d (recommended: this device has no slow cores)
SAI splits each stroke into one piece per core it sees. When it sees only the fast cores, every piece can run on a fast one. A change takes effect the next time SAI starts.
This device\'s %1$d cores by strength: %2$d fast (green), %3$d slower (yellow).
This device\'s %1$d cores by strength: none is much slower.
This device\'s %1$d cores by strength (the fastest is 100%%): %2$d fast (green), %3$d slower (yellow).
This device\'s %1$d cores by strength (the fastest is 100%%): none is much slower.
This device has %1$d fast cores and %2$d slower ones.
SAI Pen finds no slower cores on this device, so SAI can see all of them.

SAI splits every stroke into one piece per core it sees, and the stroke is done only when its slowest piece is. %1$s If SAI sees every core, some pieces run on the slow ones and the ink waits for them. If it sees only as many as the fast cores, Fast cores: Drawing puts every piece on a fast one.

In a test on a Galaxy Tab S6 Lite, SAI then needed about 30%% less of the processor for the same strokes, and the ink caught up with the pen sooner. Nothing changes in how SAI looks or draws.

SAI has the same setting itself: in SAI, Other > Options > Environment, CPU Cores Assignment C and Number of CPU Cores Used. SAI Pen does it here so you don't have to. Use one or the other, not both: while a number is chosen here, leave SAI's own setting on A, its default. To use SAI's own setting instead, choose All here.

A change takes effect the next time SAI starts.
SAI\'s brushes and textures are counted here after SAI\'s first start.

SAI keeps everything in one folder named settings: your tools and presets, brush textures, paper textures, brush shapes and scatter shapes. On a PC it is in Documents > SYSTEMAX Software Development > SAIv2 > settings. SAI Pen keeps it in the same place on this device: Documents/SYSTEMAX Software Development/SAIv2/settings.

• Bring my settings from a PC: the PC's whole settings folder replaces the one here, so SAI here has your tools, presets, textures and shapes. The current one is kept as a backup.

• Add textures and brush shapes: one texture, a few pictures or a whole pack from the internet. They are added to what SAI has; nothing is replaced. Pictures in folders named like SAI's (brushtex, papertex…) go to the right place by themselves; for others SAI Pen asks what they are.

Tools and presets only come with the PC's settings.
Bring my settings from a PC

Everything SAI had on the PC: tools, presets, brush and paper textures, brush and scatter shapes. It replaces what SAI has here; the current settings are kept as a backup.\n\nWhat to pick: a zip of the whole settings folder from the PC (Documents > SYSTEMAX Software Development > SAIv2 > settings).
Brush and paper textures, brush and scatter shapes, added to what SAI has here. Nothing is replaced.\n\nWhat to pick: a brush pack\'s zip from the internet, or .bmp pictures.

1. On the PC open Documents > SYSTEMAX Software Development > SAIv2, right-click the settings folder and choose Send to > Compressed (zipped) folder.

2. Put that zip on this device, in Downloads for example.

3. Tap Look for it, or choose the zip yourself.
No SAI settings were found on the device: no zip or folder with settings2.ssd in it, up to four folders deep. Put the zip in Downloads, or choose it yourself.
This is not a SAI settings folder: there is no settings2.ssd in it.\n\nOn the PC zip the whole settings folder from Documents > SYSTEMAX Software Development > SAIv2.
Start SAI once first: it makes its brushes and textures folder on the first start. Then add yours.
SAI\'s settings folder in Documents could not be made, so nothing can be added there. Is there space on the device?

There is nothing for SAI in this: no brush or texture pictures (.bmp) and no SAI settings folder.\n\nFor your settings from a PC, zip the settings folder from Documents > SYSTEMAX Software Development > SAIv2 on the PC and pick that zip.
Add to SAI: %1$s.\n\nPictures SAI already has under the same name stay as they are.
%1$d more pictures are in folders whose names do not say what they are, and are left out.
Browse all brushes, textures and settings

These come along when you bring your settings from a PC.
SAI Pen is free, SAI is not

SAI Pen is free and open source: a fan project, made with love. It is not made by SYSTEMAX and does not include SAI.

PaintTool SAI is SYSTEMAX's program. Without a licence it works as a trial: you can draw, but not save or open files. To save your drawings, buy a SAI licence from SYSTEMAX (one payment, no subscription). It also supports the people who make SAI, so that it keeps getting better.

Already have a licence for your PC? You don't buy it again: make a certificate for this device's System ID on systemax.jp (in SAI: Other, System ID).

This is a whole SAI settings folder, from a PC or another device. Its tools, presets, brushes and textures replace the ones SAI has on this device.\n\nThe current ones are kept in Documents/SYSTEMAX Software Development/SAIv2, in a folder named %1$s.
Added to SAI: %1$s. Start SAI to use them.
Nothing new: SAI already has all of these.
%1$d were there already and stay as they were.
SAI\'s settings replaced (%1$d files). The old ones are in Documents/SYSTEMAX Software Development/SAIv2/%2$s.
SAI\'s brushes and textures: Documents/SYSTEMAX Software Development/SAIv2/settings

No other SAI was found on the device. If you downloaded a newer one, unzip it first (as a whole folder), or choose its folder yourself.
One video per drawing, every session of it in order. Tap a picture to play it.

Delete this drawing\'s timelapse: its video and every session of it? The drawing itself stays. This cannot be undone.
SAI\'s menus. SAI has only English and Japanese. Applies the next time SAI starts.
Font for Japanese, Chinese and Korean text (layer names, file names, Japanese menus). Fonts that come with Android, nothing is downloaded. SAI\'s Text tool uses its own fonts.
About SAI Pen: gestures and where your drawings go

SAI Pen is an unofficial fan project, made by a SAI fan out of love for it: a wrapper that runs PaintTool SAI Ver.2 on Android with pen pressure. Not made, endorsed or supported by SYSTEMAX. SAI belongs to SYSTEMAX.
Puts the cursor under it; a short tap clicks
Move: scroll. Spread or pinch: zoom. Turn: rotate
Show or hide the on-screen keys (a long press on their dot hides them too)
Menu: keyboard, \"SAI Pen: licence and settings\", Exit
To type, tap the box in SAI first, then open the keyboard; close it with Android\'s Back. Change the gestures any time: hold four fingers over SAI, or Gestures on SAI Pen\'s screen.
F:\\ is Documents/SAI Drawings. Save here: it stays even if you uninstall the app.
G:\\ is your gallery (DCIM and Pictures), to open a photo or screenshot in SAI.
E:\\ is your whole device. D:\\ is Download. S:\\ is SAI\'s own folder.
C:\\ is only inside the app. Don\'t save here: your file manager can\'t see it, and uninstalling deletes it.
What SAI Pen does by itself:

SAI\'s Save As starts on C:\\, so it is easy to save there by mistake. When you close SAI (and before it starts again), drawings in C:\\users\\xuser and its Desktop, Documents and Pictures are copied to Documents/SAI Drawings. The original stays, so SAI\'s Recent list still works, and nothing is overwritten: a taken name becomes \"name (2)\".
PNG and JPG pictures show up in the Gallery, album SAI Drawings. .sai2 files are in My Files only.
Timelapse videos go to Documents/SAI Drawings/Timelapses, album Timelapses.
Without a licence, SAI runs but does not save. The SAI licence is bought on SYSTEMAX\'s official website: systemax.jp/en/sai.
\"SAI Pen: licence and settings\" in the four-finger menu closes SAI: save your drawing first.
SAI keeps your brush settings only when it is closed properly, with File > Exit.
Everything too small or too big? In SAI: Window > Scaling of User Interface.
This device has %1$d GB of memory, so closing other apps matters even more.

SAI is made for PCs. Here its code is translated while it runs, so it needs a lot of memory and a fast processor, most of all on a device that isn\'t one of the most powerful (under 8 GB of memory, a slower processor).
While you draw, keep only SAI Pen open. Close the browser, games, videos and other drawing apps: they take memory, SAI slows down, and Android may even close SAI.
If Android closes SAI, anything unsaved is lost and SAI forgets your brushes and layout. Save often.
Still slow? Lower \"SAI\'s screen sharpness\" on SAI Pen\'s screen, use a smaller canvas and the plain round brush.
No drawings yet. In SAI, save to drive F: and they show up here.

Hover the pen over it to play it here.
This can\'t be undone: the files leave Documents/SAI Drawings for good, there is no bin for this folder. Their timelapses stay.
